name: ashby
label: Ashby
note: Ashby's recruiting API, which reads the key as the HTTP Basic username with a blank password, which is what we send. Every Ashby endpoint is a POST, including the ones that only read, so the path above answers 401 to an unauthenticated GET rather than data to an authenticated one.

name: boldsign
label: BoldSign
note: BoldSign's e-signature API with an API key read from X-API-KEY. BoldSign also accepts OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens, which are a different credential and are not what this entry sends.

name: bonusly
label: Bonusly
note: Bonusly's recognition API with a personal access token; call it as /gw/bonusly/api/v1/bonuses. Bonusly caps a token's life at 365 days and requires an expiry, so a stored key here stops working on a date the customer chose.

name: checkr
label: Checkr
note: Checkr's background-check API, which reads the secret key as the HTTP Basic username with an empty password, which is what we send. Checkr's staging environment is a different host and needs an upstream naming it.

name: checkr-staging
label: Checkr (staging)
note: Checkr's staging environment, named beside the production host in Checkr's own documentation, for a key that must never reach a real background check. A production key does not resolve here.

name: clockify
label: Clockify
note: Clockify's time-tracking API on the global host, which reads the key from X-Api-Key. Clockify's regional hosts for the EU, UK, USA and Australia are separate addresses a key issued there needs an upstream for, and its reports and PTO APIs live on further hosts of their own.

name: connecteam
label: Connecteam
note: Connecteam's deskless-workforce API, which reads the key from X-API-KEY. A Connecteam key is scoped to the features it was issued for, so an object outside that scope answers 403 with a valid key.

name: documenso
label: Documenso
note: Documenso's hosted v2 API, which reads the token as the whole Authorization header with no scheme word in front of it. Its v1 API is deprecated, and a self-hosted Documenso is a different address that needs an upstream naming it.

name: documenso-staging
label: Documenso (staging)
note: Documenso's staging environment, named beside the production host in Documenso's own authentication page. A token issued on the hosted production instance does not resolve here.

name: dropbox-sign
label: Dropbox Sign
note: Dropbox Sign, still served from its HelloSign host, reads the key as the HTTP Basic username with a blank password, which is what we send. Its OAuth flow for acting on another account's behalf issues a different credential that this entry does not carry.

name: everhour
label: Everhour
note: Everhour's time-tracking API, which reads the key from X-Api-Key. Everhour also accepts the key in a query string, which we never do because a credential in a URL reaches logs and receipts.

name: factorial
label: Factorial
note: Factorial's HR API, which reads the key from x-api-key; the version is a date in the path, so call it as /gw/factorial/api/2025-01-01/resources/... . Factorial's own documentation says an API key has total access to the whole company and never expires, and that marketplace integrations must use OAuth instead.

name: greenhouse
label: Greenhouse (Harvest)
note: Greenhouse's Harvest API, which reads the token as the HTTP Basic username with a blank password, which is what we send. Greenhouse's Job Board API needs no credential and its Ingestion and Onboarding APIs are separate hosts and separate keys.

name: harvest
label: Harvest
note: Harvest's v2 time-tracking and invoicing API with a personal access token. One token reaches every Harvest and Forecast account the person has, so Harvest requires a Harvest-Account-Id header to say which one — we do not set it, and the caller's own request has to carry it.

name: homebase
label: Homebase
note: Homebase's scheduling and timesheet API for hourly teams, with a bearer token issued to a partner account. Homebase issues API access on request rather than from the account settings, so a customer without one has nothing to paste here.

name: humaans
label: Humaans
note: Humaans' HR API with a personal access token; call it as /gw/humaans/api/people. The token carries the permissions of the person who created it, so it reaches no more of the directory than they can see.

name: kombo
label: Kombo
note: Kombo's unified HR API with a dashboard key sent as a bearer token. Every data call also needs an X-Integration-Id naming the customer's connected system, which we do not set; and a key the customer bound to an IP allowlist will refuse calls arriving from this service's egress address.

name: lattice
label: Lattice
note: Lattice's performance and engagement API with a key from the admin dashboard. This is the United States host; a customer whose Lattice data is held in EMEA answers at api.emea.latticehq.com and is the lattice-emea entry.

name: lattice-emea
label: Lattice (EMEA)
note: Lattice for a customer whose data Lattice holds in EMEA, named as the region's host in Lattice's own documentation. The token and its placement are identical to the lattice entry and only the host differs.

name: lever
label: Lever
note: Lever's Data API, which reads the key as the HTTP Basic username with a blank password, which is what we send. Lever's sandbox is a different host, and its Postings API for a public job board takes no credential at all.

name: merge
label: Merge
note: Merge's unified API, whose category is part of the path — /api/hris/v1 for HR, and the same key covers its other categories. Every request also needs an X-Account-Token naming the linked end customer, which we do not set, so the caller's own request has to carry it.

name: persona
label: Persona
note: Persona's identity-verification API with an API key from the dashboard. Persona pins behaviour to a Persona-Version header and key casing to Key-Inflection; we set neither, so the caller's own request has to carry them.

name: pinpoint
template_hint: the name in your Pinpoint address — acme in acme.pinpointhq.com
label: Pinpoint
note: Pinpoint's ATS on your own account's host, reading the key from X-API-KEY; the key is made under Settings, API and Webhooks. Pinpoint's own documentation warns the key must not be used from browser code, which this service does not change.

name: recruitee
template_hint: your company's numeric id, the number after /c/ in a Recruitee API address
label: Recruitee
note: Recruitee's ATS API for one company, with a personal API token from Settings, Apps and plugins. Recruitee's own documentation says a token carries exactly the permissions of the person who made it and that its access level cannot be narrowed, so it acts in that person's name.

name: rippling
label: Rippling
note: Rippling's REST API with an API token from the API Tokens app, sent as a bearer token. What the token reaches is fixed by the scopes chosen when it was made and by the permissions of the admin who made it, and Rippling revokes it if that person leaves or it goes unused for thirty days.

name: signaturit
label: Signaturit
note: Signaturit's v3 e-signature API with the production access token from your account. Signaturit's sandbox is a separate host with its own token and is the signaturit-sandbox entry; a production token does not work there or the other way round.

name: signaturit-sandbox
label: Signaturit (sandbox)
note: Signaturit's sandbox, named beside the production host throughout Signaturit's own reference, for a token that must never reach a real signature request. Nothing signed here is legally binding.

name: signwell
label: SignWell
note: SignWell's e-signature API, which reads the key from X-Api-Key; call it as /gw/signwell/api/v1/documents. SignWell's API applications for acting on another account's behalf use a separate key that this entry does not carry.

name: talentlms
template_hint: the name in your TalentLMS address — acme in acme.talentlms.com
label: TalentLMS
note: TalentLMS on your own portal's host, reading the key as the HTTP Basic username with a blank password, which is what we send. Only a super administrator can turn API access on and see the key, and a portal with it switched off answers 403 to a key that is otherwise valid.

name: teachable
label: Teachable
note: Teachable's API, which reads the key from an apiKey header rather than Authorization. Only a school owner can create the key, so an instructor or an admin has nothing to paste here.

name: timely
label: Timely
note: Timely's time-tracking API with a key generated under Settings, Integrations. Every endpoint but /1.1/accounts carries the workspace's numeric account id in its path, so the caller has to know that id; the key alone does not imply it.

name: timetastic
label: Timetastic
note: Timetastic's holiday-booking API with the token from your Timetastic account page; call it as /gw/timetastic/api/holidays. The token is one person's and carries exactly their permissions, and Timetastic rate-limits it to five requests a second.

name: workable
template_hint: the name in your Workable address — acme in acme.workable.com
label: Workable
note: Workable's SPI v3 on your own account's host, with an access token from Workable's integrations settings. The token's scopes are fixed when it is issued, so a call outside them is refused by Workable rather than by us, and Workable does not support CORS, which rules out calling it from a browser.
